channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Haddad: "Que a polícia esclareça o que Lulinha fez e o que Flávio fez"
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), running for governor of São Paulo, called for police to investigate both the Lulinha and Flávio Bolsonaro cases but argued they are different: Flávio allegedly has ties to pension fund money, while Lulinha shows no evidence of public contracts. Haddad also referenced a São Paulo city hall wi-fi contract probe and admitted electoral difficulties, saying the centrão has rallied behind Tarcísio, making a runoff mathematically unfeasible.

item.title: Janja diz que falas de Renan Santos são 'misóginas'; candidato rebate: 'Mulheres não são desagradáveis. Ela é que é'
item.description: First lady Janja da Silva condemned statements by presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão), who during a Band debate suggested Lula would need to drink to cope with his wife. Janja labeled the attacks as misogynistic and said this is not an isolated incident. Renan fired back saying 'women aren't unpleasant, Janja is' and accused the first lady of interfering in government without being elected.

item.title: Lula lidera no 1º turno em Alagoas, diz Quaest
item.description: Quaest poll in Alagoas shows Lula (PT) leading with 44% of voting intentions in the first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 29%. In a scenario with Pablo Marçal, Lula rises to 45% and Flávio to 30%. Lula's government approval in the state stands at 52%.

item.title: Omar Aziz diz não ver resistência à PEC que acaba com 6×1 no Senado e prevê votação em 2 de setembro
item.description: Senator Omar Aziz states there is no organized resistance against the PEC ending the 6×1 work schedule and expects a vote in the CCJ on September 2nd. He will keep the text approved by the Chamber, establishing a 40-hour weekly workday with two paid rest days.

item.title: Transporte gratuito no dia da eleição deve garantir acesso ao voto
item.description: The Supreme Court ruled in 2023 for free public transport with normal frequency on election day to ensure voting access. Reducing fleet constitutes an electoral crime with detention penalty. The measure aims to include poor, rural, indigenous, and riverside voters, essential for democratic legitimacy.

item.title: Crusoé: Flávio faz campanha para Padre Kelmon
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro recorded a video endorsing the campaign of Father Kelmon (PL), a candidate for federal deputy in São Paulo. The material has already started circulating on the candidate's social media, following the official launch of his campaign on Saturday the 22nd.

item.title: Durigan destaca contenção de gastos e superávit para orçamento de 2027
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated the 2027 budget forecasts a primary surplus with mandatory spending growth below the fiscal framework limit. He advocated containing mandatory expenses to expand discretionary investments, along with reviewing tax benefits and zeroing IPI via decree.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas: Só 15 minutos de trabalho do Mansueto Almeida já resolve questão fiscal
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) stated his administration has major concerns about Brazil's fiscal situation and argued the issue must be clearly addressed in the presidential election. The remarks were made during a sabatina at the ABDIB 2026 Elections Forum in São Paulo.

item.title: Oposição joga no medo e no terror com a economia, como em 2022, afirma Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad accuses the opposition of repeating the strategy of exploiting fear regarding the economy, which was used against Lula in 2022. He made the statement in an interview with Veja magazine.

item.title: Embaixador de Trump afirma que não vai interferir na eleição do Brasil
item.description: The U.S. ambassador-designate, Daniel Pérez, stated he will not interfere in Brazil's October presidential elections. He emphasized that the election outcome is up to Brazilians and that he will work with whoever wins. His appointment remains stalled due to ongoing diplomatic tensions between the two governments.

item.title: Embaixador nomeado por Trump afirma que ‘vai trabalhar com quem vencer eleição no Brasil’
item.description: Trump-nominated ambassador Daniel Perez stated he will not interfere in Brazilian elections and will work with the winner. He emphasized U.S. economic interests and diplomatic engagement, denying interference. Lula's government rejects the nomination, while Trump retaliates with visa restrictions.

item.title: ‘O Centrão aderiu em peso ao Tarcísio’, diz Haddad em sabatina de VEJA
item.description: In an interview, Fernando Haddad (PT) stated that the Centrão bloc has largely backed Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) in São Paulo, unlike at the federal level where parties like PSD, MDB, and PP remained neutral. The PT candidate also argued that a runoff in São Paulo is 'mathematically unfeasible' given the polarization between just two candidates. Haddad said he intends to focus his campaign on education, public safety, and health, areas he claims have deteriorated under the current administration.

item.title: Tarcísio chama privatização da Sabesp de projeto “mais transformador”
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas called the privatization of Sabesp the most transformative project of his administration, noting that 2 million people gained access to drinking water and 4 million to sanitation since July 2024. He dismissed critics as lacking detailed knowledge of the issue, while Fernando Haddad opposes the privatization and advocates for reviewing post-desestatization contracts.

item.title: Smart Sampa vai identificar agressores que descumprem medidas protetivas
item.description: The São Paulo City Hall and the São Paulo State Public Ministry signed an agreement to use Smart Sampa cameras to identify and notify aggressors with active protective orders, addressing the 37% of cases not located by court officers. The system will allow the Metropolitan Civil Guard to approach offenders on the streets, supported by recent STJ rulings, and the agreement is set to be extended to the state government.

item.title: Zema afirma que STF se tornou 'balcão de negócios', propõe mudança no comando do Congresso e diz o que não privatizaria
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) stated that the Supreme Court has become a 'business counter' for some justices and proposed changes in Congress governance to prevent the Chamber and Senate presidents from blocking bills supported by parliamentarians. The candidate detailed his privatization plan, excluding Caixa, Embrapa, and IBGE, but including BNDES, Banco do Brasil, and Petrobras, the latter to be split regionally.

item.title: Análise: sabatina mostra que quanto mais entra em cena o Brasil concreto, menos mínimo fica o Estado proposto por Zema
item.description: Analysis of Romeu Zema's (NOVO/MG) interview with O Globo, Valor, and CBN reveals contradictions between his minimalist-state rhetoric and concrete defense of social programs, healthcare, and education. The candidate backtracked on privatizing Caixa Econômica and Embrapa, acknowledging the social role of state-owned enterprises and proposing demographic criteria for resource distribution. The text highlights that middle-class voters want state efficiency without giving up essential public services, leaving Zema facing the dilemma of defining which expenses to cut.

item.title: Dia do Soldado em Brasília tem Lula, Fachin e robô; veja imagens
item.description: President Lula attended the Soldier's Day ceremony at the Army Headquarters in Brasília, accompanied by Supreme Court Justices Edson Fachin and Gilmar Mendes, and Senator Hamilton Mourão. The event featured a uniformed robot and highlighted a female general, cited by Lula as progress against sexism in the military.

item.title: Disputa em Alagoas: MDB questiona registro da candidatura de Marina JHC ao Senado
item.description: The MDB in Alagoas challenges before the TRE-AL the registration of Marina JHC's Senate candidacy, alleging she failed to meet the deadline for incompatibility of her role at the Jayme de Altavila Foundation. The coalition argues that Marina continued institutional activities and public programs beyond the legal deadline, potentially violating electoral law. The case is under analysis and Marina has been summoned to submit a defense within seven days.

item.title: Campanhas políticas não têm substância
item.description: The Brazilian electoral campaign has lost ground to substantive debates, with judicial decisions and PF investigations dominating the race. Polarization is driven more by pro-Bolsonaro vs anti-Bolsonaro alignments than political proposals. The STF and PF directly influence election dynamics.

item.title: Haddad ironiza profecia de Guedes, critica Milei e defende economia do Brasil
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), candidate for governor of São Paulo, mocked Paulo Guedes's 2022 prophecy that Brazil would 'become Venezuela' under Lula, claiming the hysteria is repeating for the third time. The former minister compared Brazil's economy favorably to Milei-led Argentina, highlighting lower inflation, lower unemployment, and Brazil's exit from the Hunger Map, while attacking the opposition for 'spreading terror.' Haddad defended investments in the Brazilian economy and a development horizon ahead.

item.title: A repercussão de Zema nas redes após sabatina no JN
item.description: Romeu Zema's (Novo) interview on Jornal Nacional generated over 2 million interactions on social media, according to Nexus data. Between 8pm on Monday and 9am on Tuesday, 43% of online discourse about the candidate referenced the interview. The analysis highlights significant digital engagement with the presidential hopeful following the televised appearance.

item.title: Douglas Ruas muda tom em entrevista, ataca ‘pessoal da esquerda’ e ‘galera dos direitos humanos’ e critica Lula
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL) hardened his rhetoric in a pro-Bolsonaro interview, attacking the 'left', 'human rights crowd', and the PSB over ADPF 635, blaming it for Rio's crime surge. He criticized Lula's remarks on drug traffickers and labeled Eduardo Paes a 'Lula soldier', pledging direct confrontation with organized crime despite potential for increased police lethality.

item.title: Haddad promete ‘pente-fino’ em contratos de SP, mas diz que reestatizar Sabesp é ‘muito difícil’
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), candidate for governor of São Paulo, pledged a comprehensive review ('pente-fino') of state contracts and privatizations, including Sabesp, CPTM, and Free Flow toll systems, at the start of a potential administration. He stated that re-nationalizing Sabesp would be 'very difficult' but advocated for contract revisions to prevent the company from becoming 'a Veolia of water services.' Haddad also criticized the Tarcísio administration, citing fiscal deficits of R$ 12 billion in 2024 and a projected R$ 9 billion in 2025.

item.title: Flávio tem 52% contra 42% de Lula em eventual 2º turno no RS, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll in Rio Grande do Sul shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 52% against Lula's 42% in a hypothetical runoff. In the first round, both are tied, and Lula's approval rating in the state stands at 43%.

item.title: “Vai ser cumprida”, diz Tarcísio sobre ordem de Dino no caso ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas confirmed that the São Paulo Civil Police will comply with Justice Minister Flávio Dino's order from the Supreme Court regarding investigations into the production company of the film 'Dark Horse', based on Jair Bolsonaro's trajectory. The governor emphasized that judicial orders will always be respected.

item.title: Sabatina GLOBO/CBN/Valor: Veja como foi a entrevista com Romeu Zema em cinco pontos
item.description: In a sabatina, Romeu Zema (Novo) continued attacks on the STF, citing cases involving Moraes and Toffoli as examples of impunity. He reaffirmed criticism of Flávio Bolsonaro in the Master case and refused to back down despite internal friction. On security, he cited El Salvador under Bukele as a model to observe but denied wanting to copy the state of exception.

item.title: Brasil e EUA retomam negociação sobre o tarifaço em reunião na próxima segunda
item.description: Brazil and the U.S. resume negotiations on tariffs in a virtual meeting next Monday. Brazil aims to expand the list of exempt products before discussing the reversal of measures. The meeting was arranged after a call between Lula and Trump.

item.title: A certeza do general Mourão após encontro com Lula em Brasília
item.description: During a military ceremony for Soldier's Day, President Lula made a request to Senator Hamilton Mourão, former vice-president under Jair Bolsonaro. The full article content is restricted to subscribers.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que oposição “desrespeita” polícia de SP em caso Dark Horse
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas labeled opposition accusations that the State Civil Police is delaying the 'Operation Wi-Fi' investigation as "disrespect." The probe involves alleged fraud in contracts linked to the 'Dark Horse' film about Jair Bolsonaro. Tarcísio defended the force as a "state police, not a government police" and confirmed compliance with the Supreme Court order to transfer case data to the Federal Police within 5 days.

item.title: Haddad: ‘Nós temos de evitar que a Sabesp se transforme numa Enel das águas’
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) stated he will review state contracts and criticized the privatization of Sabesp, fearing it may become like Enel. He highlighted the deterioration of public accounts and advocated for a development plan including fiscal cleanup. He also rejected criticism of the federal economy, acknowledging challenges without being overly optimistic.

item.title: Associação cobra de presidenciáveis investimento de R$ 20 bilhões para transportes sobre trilhos
item.description: ANPTrilhos will deliver a letter to presidential candidates requesting R$ 20 billion in annual investments to expand the rail transport network, more than double the current budget of R$ 6.8 billion. The association also demands a permanent national rail mobility policy with fairer fares and integrated metropolitan governance. The event in Brasília will gather representatives from the campaigns of Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Caiado, while Zema and Renan Santos have not yet confirmed their attendance.

item.title: Sem transmissão de evento, Lula fala a jornalistas, mas evita perguntas
item.description: Lula spoke about defense investments and the inclusion of women in the Army during the Soldier's Day ceremony but avoided press questions regarding investigations involving his former chief of staff and his son. The event was attended by authorities, including STF ministers and Senator Hamilton Mourão.

item.title: Defesa de Lulinha conversa com PF e MJ para reclamar de "vazamentos"
item.description: The defense team of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, met with Justice Minister Wellington César Lima e Silva and Federal Police director-general Andrei Rodrigues to complain about leaks of confidential information from the Supreme Court investigations involving President Lula's eldest son. Attorney Marco Aurélio de Carvalho expressed concern over the media exposure of the case and requested updates on the inquiries into the leaks themselves. President Lula had previously met with the lawyer, and Justice André Mendonça ordered the Federal Police to investigate new suspected leaks in a probe examining alleged influence trafficking and mediation of interests linked to cannabidiol-based medicines.

item.title: Empresário do "grupo do golpe" doa para vereador aliado de Paes no Rio
item.description: Businessman Ivan Wrobel, investigated by Federal Police in 2022 for alleged coup-related WhatsApp messages, donated R$ 1,064 to councilman Pedro Duarte (PSD), ally of Eduardo Paes. His son Flávio made identical donation plus R$ 30,000 to PSD state directory. Duarte switched from Novo to PSD in 2026, distancing from Bolsonarism.

item.title: Mulher de Flávio adota cachorro que senador ganhou em comício
item.description: Fernanda Bolsonaro, wife of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, adopted Chiquinho, a dog he received during his campaign launch rally. The animal was rescued from abuse in July 2026 with support from the Civil Police and Alerj. The adoption was announced in a video classified as electoral propaganda, referencing the Lei Sansão against animal abuse.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que Polícia cumprirá decisão do STF e enviará à PF provas sobre ONG ligada a 'Dark Horse'
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas confirmed São Paulo Civil Police will comply with Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino's order to share evidence from Operation Wi-Fi with Federal Police regarding entrepreneur Karina Gama, producer of the 'Dark Horse' film about Bolsonaro. Tarcísio rejected accusations of politically motivated investigation delays, defending state police professionalism.

item.title: TSE: divergência em filiação não barrava registro de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The technical area of Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) concluded that the inconsistency in Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's party affiliation would not prevent his presidential candidacy registration, despite a system glitch showing him switching from PL to Missão. TSE President Nunes Marques ordered the change disregarded and freed access to the CANDex system, allowing the registration request on August 13. Flávio's defense claims he never requested the party switch.

item.title: Haddad compara casos de Lulinha e Vorcaro e diz que investigações devem ‘ir até o final’
item.description: Fernando Haddad compared the investigations into Lulinha and Flávio Bolsonaro, stating that the two cases are different and advocating for the investigations to proceed to their conclusion. He emphasized that there is no evidence of Lula acting to benefit anyone, while Flávio's case involves contracts and pension fund resources.

item.title: Próximo debate presidencial: data, horário e onde assistir
item.description: The next 2026 presidential debate will take place on September 14th at 10pm, organized by the 'A Hora da Decisão' consortium formed by VEJA and ten other media outlets. Six candidates are confirmed: Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, Zema, Renan Santos, and Augusto Cury. Following this, Record will hold a debate on 09/27 and Globo on 10/01, the last before the first round.

item.title: Governos do Brasil e dos EUA marcam reunião para avançar em negociações sobre tarifaço
item.description: Brazilian Development Minister Márcio Elias Rosa and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer scheduled a virtual meeting to advance negotiations on U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods. The meeting follows a phone call between Presidents Lula and Trump, who agreed to resume technical talks. Goals include expanding tariff exemptions and discussing reversal of the tariff measures.

item.title: MPE pede impugnação de candidato de Lula por cargo em sindicato do ABC
item.description: The Regional Electoral Prosecutor requested the impugnation of Moisés Selerges' candidacy, former president of the ABC Metalworkers Union, for allegedly missing the incompatibility deadline. The defense argues the union is privately funded, exempting him from the rule, and challenges the lawsuit's timeliness.

item.title: ‘Defesa não é pra quando sobrar dinheiro’, diz Lula em aceno a militares
item.description: Lula advocated for increased Armed Forces investments during the Soldier's Day event, stating defense cannot depend on budget leftovers. The gesture follows a R$ 4.3 billion budget freeze at the Defense Ministry and occurs amid diplomatic tensions with the US over military presence in Latin America.

item.title: Campanha de Lula cria jingle em ofensiva contra Flávio Bolsonaro para espalhar nas redes
item.description: Lula's campaign released an offensive jingle targeting Flávio Bolsonaro, referencing his request for money from Daniel Vorcaro, a R$ 6 million mansion purchase, and the imprisonment of former president Jair Bolsonaro for coup attempt. The song, inspired by a 2016 meme, is distributed via PT-affiliated networks across WhatsApp, Twitter, and TikTok. Flávio's team has not commented.

item.title: Renan Santos vai à evento em SP com Lulinha estampado na camiseta
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) wore a T-shirt featuring Lulinha's face with the phrase 'where is the elderly's money?' at the ABDIB 2026 Election Forum in São Paulo, referencing STF investigations against President Lula's eldest son. At the event, Renan criticized the electoral format, the Lula government, the Bolsonaro family, and First Lady Janja, stating Brazil lives in a 'half democracy' based on vote-buying and parliamentary amendment corruption.

item.title: PT abre vaquinha virtual para campanha de Lula
item.description: The PT launched a virtual crowdfunding campaign to finance Lula's reelection bid, accepting donations from R$13 to R$1,064. The funds complement the R$615 million allocated to the party through the Electoral Fund.

item.title: O que Flávio Bolsonaro já disse sobre o caso Dark Horse
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro gave contradictory statements regarding the accountability of the film 'Dark Horse', funded with R$61 million from banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master. Flávio is a presidential candidate for the PL party.

item.title: Renan Santos critica emendas: 'Congresso não se importa com nenhum tema nacional', diz
item.description: Renan Santos criticized parliamentary amendments, stating that the National Congress ignores national issues and focuses only on amendments. He advocates for stricter oversight of these funds during a press conference in São Paulo.

item.title: Brasil e EUA marcam nova reunião para falar sobre tarifaço
item.description: Brazil and the US scheduled a virtual meeting for Monday to discuss tariffs imposed by Washington. The meeting follows a phone call between Lula and Trump last week.

item.title: Lula vai faltar à cúpula dos Brics na Índia em setembro
item.description: President Lula will not attend the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi in September due to the proximity of the Brazilian elections and will be represented by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira. The meeting marks Xi Jinping's first visit to India in seven years and the return of Vladimir Putin, who avoided Brazil in 2025 due to an ICC arrest warrant.

item.title: Lei Antifacção no STF: juristas e MP debatem impactos em garantias fundamentais
item.description: The STF is debating the Anti-Facilitation Law (Law No. 15.358/2026) in a public hearing, with jurists warning of risks to fundamental rights, such as automatic preventive detention and restrictions on political rights. The Public Prosecutor’s Office is divided: most oppose removing homicide cases linked to criminal organizations from the Jury Court, while others view the law’s electoral impacts favorably.
